clos.original_description: Understanding how search engines work: Students should be able to explain the underlying technology behind search engines, including the algorithms used to crawl, index and rank web pages.
clos.enriched_description: Explain how search engines work, including information retrieval and web search concepts, search engine architecture, crawling and document acquisition, text processing, inverted indexes and index construction, query processing, and ranking with Boolean, proximity, vector-space, probabilistic, BM25, language-model, and learning-to-rank retrieval models.

clos.original_description: Search engine optimization: Students should be able to apply best practices for optimizing web pages to improve their visibility in search engine results pages (SERPs).
clos.enriched_description: Apply SEO best practices to improve search engine results page visibility, including content quality, site architecture, HTML factors, trust, links, user-related factors, spam and ranking updates, special collections, and the role of search engine providers.

clos.original_description: Keyword research: Students should be able to conduct keyword research to identify the most relevant and profitable keywords by using popular retrieval models..
clos.enriched_description: Conduct keyword research to identify the most relevant and profitable keywords by using popular retrieval models.
review_notes: Mapped topics do not directly support practical keyword research proficiency. The retrieval-model phrase is preserved from the original CLO, but no topic-supported enrichment was added.

clos.original_description: Analytics and tracking: Students should be able to use analytics tools to track website traffic, user behavior, and campaign performance.
clos.enriched_description: Use analytics tools to track website traffic, user behavior, and campaign performance.
review_notes: Mapped topics focus on indexing, retrieval models, classification, clustering, and search evaluation rather than analytics tools, website traffic, user behavior, or campaign performance. No topic-supported enrichment was added.

clos.original_description: Solving problems: Students should be able to apply search engine techniques to solve the real-life problems
clos.enriched_description: Apply search engine techniques to real-life problems involving social search, user tags and manual indexing, community-based question answering, collaborative searching, filtering and recommending, peer-to-peer search, metasearch, feature-based retrieval, term-dependence models, XML and entity search, longer-question answering, and multimedia search.
